newsitem.title: UK: BA and BMA halt Levant franchise plan.
newsitem.headline: BA and BMA halt Levant franchise plan.

text.p: British Airways and the privately owned British Mediterranean Airways (BMA) said Monday that they will not be proceeding with their proposed franchise agreeement because it had not been possible for BMA to meet all the conditions of the agreement.

In August BA had said that under the franchise agreement BMA would have taken over BA's services to Beirut, Amman and Damascus from October 27. A press statement Monday did not say why the agreement had fallen through. Under such a franchise BMA planes would have been repainted in BA colours and aircrew would wear BA uniforms.
Both airlines have carried cargo in belly capacity. One freight forwarders familiar said the BMA routes were well booked and carrying a high load.

British Airways will continue to operate in its own right from London Heathrow four Boeing 767-300s a week to Amman with an 8.7 tonne cargo capacity of which two will go via Beirut and two via Damascus. A BA spokesman said that while the cargo carried on the routes is relatively small, volumes are building up with produce from Amman a notable feature.
BMA which flies an Airbus Industrie A-320 will continue to operate five services from Heathrow to the Levant. All operate to Beirut with three continuing to Amman and two to Damascus.

Other expansion plans for BMA announced in August as part of the franchise would have seen an expansion of the service to Alexandria in December and then to Georgia, Kyrgystan and Uzebekistan in the summer of 1997. But spokesmen for both airlines said these plans were now on hold. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
